name: Muldoons excavated channel
summary: A forked channel cut through basalt at Lake Condah by Gunditjmara people, shown by dated infill to have existed by about 4650 BCE.
description: Bifurcated channel F10 created by removal of basalt blocks; dated basal infill establishes an earlier excavated form.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

impact.note: One cut channel that gave one community engineered fish trapping, a new capability for them, with later walls built onto it.

date.label: by c. 4650 BCE
date.basis: Rounded combined calibrated ranges of basal infill samples OZL608/OZL760, c. 6450–6740 cal BP (BP=1950), constrain prior excavation. This dates evidence of an existing channel, not its invention.

events.statement: Bifurcated channel F10 created by removal of basalt blocks; dated basal infill establishes an earlier excavated form.
events.caveats: Construction may be older. Charcoal association, old wood and stratigraphic interpretation limit precision; only F10 is represented.

evidence.supports: Basalt removal, basal infill and minimum-age interpretation.

date.label: by c. 1350 CE (inferred)
date.basis: The authors date construction and initial use of the later walled F10 channel approximately c. 1150–1350 CE (600–800 cal BP), based on sediment mixing.

events.statement: Archaeological interpretation places initial use of F10 with its later walls within c. 1150–1350 CE.
applications: water management within the F10 fishery complex
events.population: Gunditjmara users of the Muldoons F10 water channel
events.caveats: This approximate archaeological interpretation is not a hard upper bound, a directly witnessed catch or proof of uninterrupted use since the much older basal infill. The source was inspected online; no local copy could be retained in the current pass.

evidence.supports: The authors distinguish earlier F10 excavation from later walls, and infer construction and initial use of the walled channel around 600–800 cal BP.

earliest_record.rationale: Historian/date dispute retained. A later community witness is not an automatic earliest-record anchor.

community_entry.community: Gunditjmara users of the Muldoons F10 water channel

community_entry.proxy_reason: Use is an archaeological interpretation of the later constructed water-channel context; it does not convert the much older infill date into an observed fishing-use date.
